To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cyaA gene of B. bronchisepticac encodes an AC-Hly protein that is very similar to the one encoded by B. pertussisc but that it has some differences, mainly in the C-terminal region of the protein.
we have cloned and sequenced the Bb AC-Hly gene, and that it is highly homologous to the Bp AC-Hly gene.
the B. bronchisepti cyaA gene, encoding the adenylactylase-hemolysis (AC-Hly) toxin, was cloned, sequenced and compared with that of B. pertussi s.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the cyaA gene of B. bronchisepti...
the molecular characterization of Bb AC-Hly, a toxin that is closely related to Bp AC-Hly, but with some differences that might be relevant for the pathogenic properties of these two bacteria.
the molecular biology and the pathogenicity of Bordetella bronseptica and its relationship with the other bordetella species, especially Bordetella pertusis, the causative agent of whooping cough.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while the CyaA protein from Bp is a potent virulence factor, the CyaA from Bb is not.
the AC-Hly of Bb and Bp are very similar proteins.
Bb AC-Hly has a higher degree of homology with B. parapertussis AC-Hly than with Bp AC-Hly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Bb AC-Hly has a similar overall amino-acid sequence to the Bp AC-Hly but the C-terminal repeat is more similar to that from Bordetella avium and the N-terminal repeat is more variable.
the AC-Hly is encoded by a single gene in Bb as well as in Bp and that the two genes have a high degree of homology.
the AC-Hly is a protein with a molecular mass of 220 kDa that is encoded by a 6.2-kb gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Bb CyaA has a different C-terminal repeat region compared to that of Bp, but the N-terminal region of both CyaAs is highly conserved, suggesting that the N- and C-terminal parts of the AC-Hly are functionally different.
the B. bronchisepticia AC-Hly is a very good candidate for the production of an adenylate-cyclase based vector for gene delivery to eukaryotic cells.
the CyaA protein from Bb, like that of Bp, is a potent activator of adenylate cyclases.
